_readme: LUNA — ARM AND HEAD MOTION
THREE THINGS LIVE IN THIS FILE
speaking   Arm movement while she is talking. LOOPS: the poses run
start to finish, then start again, for as long as she is
speaking. The moment she stops, the arms go home.
modes      One-shot actions on the app's Mode buttons. Each plays
through once and returns home. Rename them to whatever
they actually do — HI, Handshake, Point.
nod        The head nod while she LISTENS to a question.
THE DISPLAY'S MOTION TOGGLE governs the SPEAKING gestures only — whether
she gesticulates as she talks. The Mode buttons always work: somebody
has just pressed one on purpose, and refusing it because the ambient
movement is switched off would be baffling.
ALL NUMBERS ARE APP VALUES — the same figures the display's sliders
show. Arms 0-2000, fingers 0-100.
TO CHANGE A MOVEMENT
1. Action page on the display, move the sliders until it looks right.
2. Read the numbers off the screen.
3. Type them into a pose below.
4. Save. No restart — the next gesture picks it up.
LEFT AND RIGHT ARE SEPARATE. Mirrored arms are never symmetric once
built, so a pose states each side:
{ "left":  { "elbow": 1820, "forearm": 612 },
"right": { "elbow": 1669, "forearm": 1897 },
Only name the joints that move; anything omitted stays where the
previous pose left it.
Check your edit before relying on it:
python3 -m json.tool gestures.json
TWO JOINTS AT ONCE, AND SMOOTH MOVEMENT
Several joints in ONE pose move together:
{ "left": { "forearm": 130, "elbow": 1600 }, "hold": 0.8 }
{ "left": {...}, "right": {...}, "hold": 0.8 }     both arms
BUT they do not ARRIVE together by default. The firmware moves every
joint at the same degrees per second, so at speed 700 an 870-unit
forearm sweep takes 0.65s while a 100-unit elbow nudge takes 0.08s —
the eye reads that as one joint moving and then another.
Add "glide": true and the engine sends intermediate positions so every
joint covers the same FRACTION of its own travel at each step. They
then arrive at the same instant however far each has to go:
{ "left": { "forearm": 130, "elbow": 1600 },
"hold": 0.8, "glide": true }
Glide also EASES — starting and ending slowly, which is what makes a
movement look smooth. Constant velocity reads as mechanical however
slow it is, because real limbs accelerate and decelerate.
Add "ease": false for a constant-rate glide.
COST: about ten commands per joint instead of one. Fine for a few poses
where the coordination matters; not something to put on every pose of a
twenty-second dance.

_note: Hard clamp per joint. Nothing in this file can drive a joint outside
these, so a typo cannot throw an arm.
Opened to the full 0-2000 because home is at 0 for several joints, so
a narrow band around 1000 would have made home itself unreachable.
THESE ARE NOT MEASURED STOPS. They are the app's full range, which is
the widest thing the firmware will accept. Narrow them per joint once
you know where each one binds: creep it out with the sliders, back off
the moment it strains or touches the body, and put that number here.
Until then the firmware's ARM_MIN/ARM_MAX are the only protection.
_head_note: headUD is clamped to 278-1611, which is 25-145 degrees — the
MEASURED mechanical travel of Luna's head. Outside that the servo
A sequence asking for headUD 2000 is therefore capped at 1611. That
is the top of the real range, so the head still looks fully up.
While a sequence drives the head, the head tracker stands down — it
normally owns these joints for the listening nod and for turning
towards a voice, and two writers on one joint means the head twitches.

_note: The MEASURED rest pose. Every joint here is sent the moment she stops
speaking and after every mode action, so the arms cannot drift over a
conversation.
Note lateral, shoulder and elbow are 0, NOT 1000. The earlier values
assumed 1000 was mid-travel and therefore neutral; on this robot it is
not, so every pose written around 1000 was wrong. The wrists are the
only joints that genuinely rest at mid-travel.
Head nod while LISTENING to a question. Up and down only.
amplitude is app values either side of where the head points: 35 is
about 3 degrees. Larger stops reading as attention and starts reading
as agreement. period is one full cycle in seconds.

_speed_note: Servo speed while gesturing, of 2000. LOWER IS SMOOTHER: the firmware
interpolates towards each target at this rate, so a smaller number means
more, finer steps and less visible stepping on a long sweep.
320 of 2000 is roughly 60 degrees a second — deliberate rather than
brisk. Raise it if the gestures feel sluggish; drop towards 200 if any
A mode can override this with its own "speed" value.

_note: Runs on a LOOP the whole time she is speaking an ANSWER, then the arms
go home. Fifteen steps as measured, one joint per step, alternating
arms.
Each step names only the joint that moves, so everything else holds
where the previous step left it — that is what makes the arms build up
a posture over the cycle rather than snapping between positions.
ONLY for answers: Q&A, GPT and the vision answers. Not the wake
acknowledgement, not 'Let me take a look', not the welcome message and
not reminders — see answers_only below.
Governed by the display's Motion toggle. Off means she talks without
moving; the Mode buttons still work either way.
One full cycle takes about 11 seconds. A short answer will not finish
it, which is fine: the arms simply go home from wherever they reached.
_answers_only_note: true  gesture only while speaking an answer to a question.
false gesture during any speech at all, including the wake
acknowledgement and the welcome message — which looks odd, since
'Yes?' is over before the first pose completes.
speaking._loop_pause_note: Seconds between the end of one cycle and the start of the next. 0 runs them straight together.

_note: The app's Mode buttons. It sends /mode?value=Mode 1, Mode 2, Mode 3 —
which is why the keys are named that way. The 'name' is only for the
log, so call it whatever the action actually is.
Each plays through ONCE and returns home. They do not loop.
Add more keys if the app ever sends Mode 4.

Mode 1.name: HI
_note: THE RAISE now glides. Your values are unchanged — only the grouping
and the timing differ.
Before: lateral 1100 (1.8s), THEN shoulder 1763 (0.8s), THEN elbow
2000 (1.9s) — three separate movements, each starting after the last
finished. The arm went out, then up, then straightened.
Now: lateral and shoulder glide TOGETHER, so the arm lifts and opens as
one movement, then the elbow extends. Two movements instead of three,
and both eased so they start and end gently.
The wave is deliberately NOT glided. It is a single joint, so there is
nothing to coordinate; easing would soften the snap that makes it read
as a wave; and eight glided poses would be eighty commands where eight
will do.
If the lift looks too slow, lower the holds rather than removing the
glide — a glide spends 80% of its hold travelling, so 1.6s means about
1.3s of movement.

Mode 2.name: Handshake
_note: RIGHT hand. One step per pose, as specified:
1. lateral 230
2. elbow 1537
3. elbow 2000
4. elbow 1353     the shake
5. elbow 2000
6. elbow 1583
then home.
Steps 3 to 6 are the shake itself, so they hold briefly. Add more
elbow lines to shake more times.

Mode 3.name: Vanakkam
_note: BOTH hands, moving together. As specified:
1. lateral 932
2. elbow 1877
3. forearm 595, held 10 seconds
then home.
Written as a shared value rather than separate left and right blocks,
because the numbers were taken with both arms moving together and are
the same for each. If the two arms turn out not to match once you
watch it, split any pose into left/right blocks with its own numbers.
Slower than the other modes: a greeting held for ten seconds should
arrive gently rather than snap into place.

_home_speed_note: Speed for the return to home, of 2000. Slower than the gestures on
purpose: the arms have just been somewhere deliberate, and snapping back
looks like a fault. On a full-size arm it is also the movement most

_note: The app's Run buttons. It sends /run?value=Run 1, Run 2, Run 3.
Same shape as modes: one-shot, plays through once, then home. The only
difference is which button triggers it.
A step of { "home": true } returns the arms to the rest pose PART WAY
THROUGH and waits for them to arrive — Run 1 needs it between the left
half and the right half.

Run 1.name: Lap
_note: As specified. Left side first, then home, then the right side mirrors
it and the head lifts.
right lateral 1641, right shoulder 843
left lateral 993, left forearm 374, left elbow 2000
HOME
left lateral 1641, left shoulder 843
right lateral 993, right forearm 374, right elbow 2000
headUD 2000  (capped to 1611, the top of the real travel)
hold 5s, then home
The head tracker is stood down for the duration, so its nod does not
fight the headUD step.
The app's Loop buttons — a DANCE.
intro     played ONCE, to get into position
poses     repeated for `duration` seconds, with the music
Kept separate because getting into a pose and keeping a rhythm are
different things: repeating the setup moves would make the dance lurch
back to the start every cycle instead of flowing.
MUSIC lives in  ~/pi_assistant/music/  — .wav plays with aplay, already
installed. .mp3 needs:  sudo apt install mpg123
eyes         an animation for the length of the dance, back to idle after
base_wiggle  rock the base left and right. Equal pairs, so the robot
finishes roughly where it started rather than creeping
across the room over twenty seconds.
base_speed   1-100. Low on purpose: this is a sway, not driving.

Loop 1.name: Dance 1
_note: INTRO, once:
left lateral 1117 + right lateral 1117   (one pose, so together)
left elbow 1649
right forearm 130
right elbow 2000
right forearm 1000
LOOP, for 20 seconds with the music and the base rocking:
Eight poses at 0.45s is a 3.6-second cycle, so about five and a half
repeats in 20 seconds. Short poses on purpose: this is a beat, and at a
second a pose it would read as slow waving instead.
Watch that the forearms actually REACH 130 and 1000 before each hold
expires. At speed 700 a full sweep takes roughly 0.4s, so 0.45 is close
to the limit — if the movement looks clipped, raise the holds to 0.55
or raise the speed rather than leaving it half-travelled.
The RF 140 in the seventh pose is as given, not a typo on my part.
The head moves on its OWN rhythm, in parallel with the arms —
not as extra joints in the arm poses. The forearm section runs
at 0.45s a pose; a head following that beat twitches rather than
dances, and the head carries the camera so it is the most
visible thing moving.
This track loops independently for the whole dance.
headLR 0-2000 is the full sweep; headUD is clamped to 278-1611,
which is the measured 25-145 degrees of real travel.
Holds of about a second: the head has further to travel than a
forearm and looks best arriving rather than snapping.
